title: Jacob Kiplimo reclaims half marathon world record
content:
Ugandan athlete Jacob Kiplimo has broken the half marathon world record with a 57:20 run in Lisbon, Portugal.

His run was 10 seconds quicker than the previous best time, held by Ethiopia’s Yomif Kejelcha from the 2024 Valencia half marathon.

“I’m so happy to break the world record,” Kiplimo, 25, said. “After the first 10km, I thought the world record was possible. I tried to keep pushing the pace in the final two kilometres.”

He split 13:28 for the first five kilometres and covered the first 10km in 27:00, which was on pace to dip just under 57 minutes and broke up the lead pack.

Kiplimo beat Kenyan runners Nicholas Kipkorir (58:08, second) and Gilbert Kipkosgei Kiprotich (58:59, third). Impressively five men in the race broke one hour.

Providing the record is ratified, it should prove some sort of redemption for Kiplimo. In February 2025, he clocked 56:42 — the first half marathon run in history to break 57 minutes — at the Barcelona half marathon. However World Athletics did not ratify the record because he was too close to the lead vehicle, which is considered to be pacing assistance.

Including his performance from Barcelona, Kiplimo accounts for five of the 12 instances of an athlete breaking 58 minutes for the half marathon.

He has reclaimed a world record that he held for nearly three years, with his 57:31 (also from Lisbon, in 2021) standing firm until Kejelcha went one second better in October 2024. If this record is approved, it will be the sixth revision to the men’s half marathon world record in the past eight years.

As a three-time cross country world champion, Kiplimo stepped up to the roads after winning Olympic and World Championship bronze over 10,000m in 2021 and 2022 respectively.

He is widely tipped to be one of the greatest marathoners of his generation. Kiplimo won the 2025 Chicago marathon and finished second behind Sebastian Sawe in London last April.

He will race this year’s London marathon on April 26, with his 2:02:23 personal best the second-quickest among the elite men’s field, only behind Sawe’s 2:02:05.
